To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

thrust-vectoring attachments on a rectangular nozzle decrease the sound intensity of a supersonic jet on each axis plane and that deflection of the jet flow by the thrust-vectoring attachments produces an approximately corresponding deflexion of the acoustic field.

thrust vectoring can be applied to rectangular jets without increasing the noise, and that thrust vectoring in the minor axis direction of a rectangular nozzle can deflect the noise without increasing its level.

thrust-vectoring attachments on an otherwise clean, rectangular nozzle decrease the overall intensity of sound radiating from the jet, and that the acoustic radiation pattern of the jet is deflected approximately in proportion to the thrust-vectoring deflection angle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the noise produced by a jet from a rectangular nozzle equipped with thrust-vectoring attachments.
the acoustic characteristics of high-speed jets from rectangular nozzles with thrust-vectoring attachments.

the development of a model of a rectangular nozzle with vectoring attachments, the measurement of the sound radiated from this nozzle, the measurement of flow properties of the jet issuing from the model, and the development of a computer model of the flow and sound radiation from this nozzle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of the thrust-vectoring attachments on the rectangular nozzle decreases the noise levels in the peak emission directions, but does not change the frequency spectra.
the thrust vectoring attachments on this rectangular nozzle, in the absence of any deflection, have a favorable effect on the sound radiation characteristics.
the addition of the thrust-vectoring attachments on the rectangular nozzle, with or without deflection of the nozzle, results in an overall reduction in sound pressure levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thrust-vectoring attachments have a strong effect on the acoustic field of the jet and that the effect depends strongly on the direction of observation.

the acoustic characteristics of rectangular nozzle jets with thrust-vectoring attachments can be predicted from a knowledge of the flow characteristics of a round nozzle, with a small correction factor for the minor axis plane.

the addition of a rectangular nozzle thrust-vectoring system to an otherwise clean rectangular jet does not increase noise in any direction, and that deflection of the thrust vector by the nozzle system does not significantly change the acoustic field in the peak emission region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acoustic signature of a rectangular nozzle jet can be made to be comparable to that of a circular nozzle jet with the use of thrust-vectoring.
the addition of the thrust-vectoring attachments on the rectangular nozzle decreases the sound radiation in the peak emission directions.
the addition of a thrust-vectoring capability to a rectangular nozzle does not necessarily increase the overall sound pressure level of the jet noise, and in some instances, can decrease it.
